notes.title: Sequel Announcement & more
notes.content:
Hey folks,

Even though The Suicide of Rachel Foster has already been around for a few years, 
we've still got some exciting news for you!

[h3][b]TSORF Definitive Edition for PS5[/b][/h3]

We bring to you an improved version of The Suicide of Rachel Foster for PlayStation5.

The Definitive Edition comes with
[list]
[*] A free upgrade for PS4 edition owners
[*] Upscaled textures in 60 fps and Dolby Atmos support
[*] New adaptive triggers for perfect immersion
[*] Haptic feedback & dynamic vibrations
[*] An additionally available artbook
[/list]
But the news don't end here...

[h3][b]The Fading of Nicole Wilson[/b][/h3]

Years ago, Nicole Wilson found out about the tragic fate of Rachel. But what happened to Nicole?

[b]Now Nicole's story continues.[/b]

We are very excited to let you know that you can now 
[b]wishlist the upcoming sequel "The Fading of Nicole Wilson"[/b]!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2947700/The_Fading_of_Nicole_Wilson/

We are celebrating these news with a thrilling 90% discount on The Suicide of Rachel Foster,
so everybody can refresh their and Nicole's memory or experience the story for the first,
spinechilling time!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1057750/The_Suicide_of_Rachel_Foster/

We hope you share our excitement about us working on this new title.

Until next time,
One-O-One Games and Daedalic Entertainment

notes.title: New Language and Polishing Patch
notes.content:
Heyho everyone,

You might be wondering - Why is there a ~7gb patch for The Suicide of Rachel Foster? Don't worry, we just can't get enough of it! For any Japanese, Korean, or Polish players who haven't had the chance to play yet due to the language, the barriers have been lifted!

Additionally to adding those 3 languages, we did some general polishing and stabilisation.

Best Regards!

notes.title: Now also on Nintendo Switch!
notes.content:
[b][i]Welcome back to the Timberline Hotel. We hope that you enjoy your stay![/i][/b]

We are happy to announce that "The Suicide of Rachel Foster" is now available on Nintendo Switch.

[previewyoutube=vRmnDKdVpsE;full][/previewyoutube]

Just in time for Halloween you can now embark on Nicoles journey everywhere you go. Revisit the Timberline from the haunted hotel of your choice - or the comfort of your own home. 

We hope that you enjoy the game and we want to thank you for all the love over the last year and a half.

To celebrate the release, we have also created a little website where you can unlock an artbook with concept art from the production. Just look out for hints to [url=https://www.tsorf.games/uncover-the-truth/]uncover the truth[/url]!

You can find The Suicide of Rachel Foster on the Nintendo eShop here:
[b]North America[/b]: [url=https://www.nintendo.com/games/detail/the-suicide-of-rachel-foster-switch/]The Suicide of Rachel Foster on Nintendo eShop (NA)[/url]
[b]Europe[/b]: [url=https://www.nintendo.co.uk/Games/Nintendo-Switch-download-software/The-Suicide-of-Rachel-Foster-2064357.html]The Suicide of Rachel Foster on Nintendo eShop (Europe)[/url]

notes.title: We are live!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36295028/0f2c03e9f1e04380d1547e8a88737f715d971a28.jpg[/img]

[h3]The Suicide of Rachel Foster is out now![/h3]

Find yourselves trapped in an isolated mountain hotel and uncover what truly happened to Rachel Foster, a young woman who seemingly took her own life 10 years ago.

You will follow Nicole, a young woman driven by her mother’s dying wish to uncover her family's dark past. She finds herself in the dilapidated and abandoned family hotel on a snow filled mountain. Knowing her own father had a role to play in the downfall of Rachel, Nicole relies on the support of a young FEMA agent to unearth the truth once and for all.

[previewyoutube=LTXQ-ND9C2s;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: The Suicide of Rachel Foster is a Gone Home-meets-Firewatch mystery in an old hotel
notes.content:
The Suicide of Rachel Foster is an eerie-looking first-person narrative adventure game set in a "desolate mountain hotel" in the early 1990s. Trapped by a blizzard, and with no connection to the outside world beyond the disembodied voice of a distant FEMA agent, players will explore the hotel in an effort to piece together "a dark family mystery."

If that setup, and the trailer, strike you as a little familiar, the odds are good that you've played Gone Home, What Remains of Edith Finch, and/or Firewatch at some point over the past few years. The similarities are not subtle—but, on the other hand, if you're going to take inspiration from other games, you could do a lot worse than those three.

Publisher Daedalic Entertainment describes The Suicide of Rachel Foster as "a thriller about love and deception," with bits of mystery and horror here and there, all built on "intriguing, touching, and mature storytelling." Daedalic is generally pretty solid on that front, Goodbye Deponia notwithstanding, but the game is actually being developed by One-o-One Games, an Italian studio whose one previous release—a Mad Max-knockoff twin-stick shooter for mobiles—doesn't offer much insight into the depth of its narrative capabilities.

Still, I like the looks of the trailer, and I do enjoy a good mystery, so I really hope this turns out to be one. The Suicide of Rachel Foster is available for pre-purchase on Steam, and will go live on February 19.
